verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory. Advisories do not block.
acceptanceGrade: ACCEPT-WITH-ONE-ADVISORY. Application-grade for what this artifact is — a grouped measurement of ten leftover classes plus two candidate obligations — and expressly not a closure.

scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsAccepted: That DR-117's EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b, EE-6a, EE-7a, EE-7b and EE-7d have no live gate corpus; that they fall into two kinds — excluded-form admission refusal and preview install shape; and that the two proposed obligations, with their owner and claims, are the shape that would own them.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsNotAccepted: This ACCEPT does not close DR-117's leftover-design, adds no DR-G* row, assigns no gate number, changes required-now from 24, and makes DR-117 neither eligible nor SATISFIED. The token SATISFIED does not appear in the artifact at all.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatItUnblocks: Later D-000 MF-6 acts that would add named DR-G* rows for these two kinds, and separately the D-086 successor that would name EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e at G09, G14 and G16.

advisories.title: The second obligation's claim carries no corpus characterisation and no not-that-gate distinctions, where the first obligation carries both
advisories.finding: The excluded-form obligation's claim ends 'Corpus is hostile-but-well-formed admission inputs (v1-slice §7 item 8). Not G21 sandbox. Not G23 provider FactCandidate/Coverage.' The install-shape obligation's claim is four product statements with no corpus sentence and no distinction from the live gates it might be confused with. The distinguishing work exists — join v1 records that DR-101 owns core inventory only, that the second-role refusal is the D-002 and DR-118 role-list decision rather than G13's quality corpus, and that EE-7d rides nothing — and that join is pinned here as basedOn. But it sits one hop away, and every one of the five obligations in the DR-131 analogue carried its own distinguishing clause inline.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Nothing false follows, and the distinctions are recoverable from the pinned predecessor. A later act adopting the second obligation would have to define a corpus in any case, and that act gets its own review.
advisories.repair: Add one sentence to the install-shape claim: what its corpus is, and that it is not DR-101 core inventory, not DR-G13's language-quality corpus, and not the DR-131 pack identity.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The artifact carries no per-class entries, where the DR-131 admission-leftover artifact carried verbatim input and pass for each class
consideredAndDeclined.observation: A reader of this file alone sees only the two obligations and their owns lists.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The per-class reasoning was established in join v1 and this artifact pins it as basedOn with its role stated, which is how inheritance is evidenced in this corpus — the same disposition I reached for gate-harness-naming.v4's narrowed input list and for the DR-131 admission artifact's lack of per-gate reasons. I checked every one of the ten classes against v5 myself rather than relying on the absence being harmless.

consideredAndDeclined.item: EE-7d, the sidecar-deferred class, is arguably a product posture rather than a harness-testable property
consideredAndDeclined.observation: Bundling it into an install-shape gate obligation presumes a corpus can exercise it.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: v5 itself states EE-7d as a class with a pass condition and this artifact only proposes, as candidate-not-adopted, that some later obligation own it. Whether a corpus can exercise it is exactly what the adopting act must decide, and it gets its own review. Charging it here would be adjudicating the later act's design.

independence.priorParticipation: I accepted the join this artifact rests on, on the row where I once accepted a false enforcement claim. So I re-read v5's pass conditions for all ten classes rather than trusting the join's summary, and I tested the seven-class bundle against those passes rather than against the artifact's own claim sentence — because an over-bundle is exactly what I failed to catch in the first DR-133 join.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Twelve attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Read the scope before recording: this is a grouped measurement plus two candidate obligations, not a closure. All ten DR-117 leftover classes stay leftover-design, no row is added, no number is assigned, required-now stays 24, and the token SATISFIED does not appear in the artifact at all. Custody is clean: 6280d648 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left a7d98c2, file 08 at the 6d593a11 pin the artifact carries, COORD at 2f733c39, and D-155 verified adopted with a single heading. The two attacks that matter here both fail on measurement. On coverage, the union of the two owns lists is exactly join v1's leftover set with no duplicate, and EE-3a, EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e — the discharged and riding classes — appear in neither, so nothing measured as riding is swept into the proposal. On over-bundling, which is what sank the first DR-133 join, I tested the seven-class obligation against v5's own pass conditions rather than its claim sentence: EE-1, EE-2, EE-3b, EE-4, EE-5a, EE-5b and EE-6a are every one of them a hostile-but-well-formed input refused at admission or request validation with no ExecutionId, under v1-slice §7 item 8, which is the law the proposed claim names and cites. That is seven instances of one kind, not seven kinds. The second obligation's three classes are all preview install and role shape, a coherent and distinct second kind. Number discipline is clean — nothing is numbered, both G29 mentions are refusals, and the gate table is still 28 rows — the proposed owner 'Product owner' is byte-exact against DR-117's own owner column, and the leftover stands 'until later D-000 MF-6 acts add named DR-G* rows', with named doing the work that closes the condition-4 flip. The advisory is that the install-shape obligation carries no corpus sentence and no not-that-gate distinctions, where the excluded-form obligation carries both and where all five obligations in the DR-131 analogue carried one; the distinctions exist in the pinned join, so nothing is false, but the asymmetry is worth closing. Two further items are recorded as considered and declined.
